title: Ukraine wants to use AI to predict where Russian drones will hit the battlefield with 'high probability'
key_facts: Ukraine's defense ministry said on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026) that its forces are about to start using a jointly NATO-developed AI model, 'Model No. 13', to predict where and when Russia's drone strikes will land.

The tool analyzes past combat data, weather and battlefield conditions to determine with 'high probability' how Russian troops will use drones, forecasting the time, location, intensity and type of drone.
The ministry says the solution has been validated on real-world datasets and is ready for integration into the armed forces' situational awareness systems.

It was developed by Ukraine's armed forces and NATO's Allied Command Transformation, with the Joint Analysis, Training and Education Center (JATEC), which NATO created in late 2024 to learn lessons from the war.
A second joint model, No. 32, which plans artillery deployments, is still a prototype in testing.

Model No. 13 will likely run on DELTA, Ukraine's battlefield management app that combines drone, camera and battlefield reports; DELTA had over 200,000 users in November and already uses an AI module called Vezha to flag Russian equipment.
Ukrainian officials said in February that forces had been using AI and machine learning to process combat data for 'threat forecasting'.
ACT and JATEC did not immediately respond to Business Insider's requests for comment.
